content.text:
Found the answer. Here's what's happening:

**The stars only show when an offer carries a real rating, and the registry you're reviewing has none.** Specifically:

- Your `.env.local` only has OpenAI and Deepgram keys. No Amazon PA-API, Walmart, or Target credentials are set up, so every product in your newer registries comes from the app's built-in hand-checked catalog (`lib/retail/catalog.json`) or a plain "search this store" link. Neither carries star ratings.
- The catalog offers in your saved registries do have numbers stored (4.2 / 4.5), but those are old price-tier placeholders, not customer ratings — `components/ProductRating.tsx:5` deliberately ignores them, which is exactly why you were seeing the "Read reviews at Amazon" fallback text before. Once I removed that text per your request, offers like these show nothing at all.
- Your review page loads offers saved at registry creation; it doesn't re-fetch ratings. (Side note: the two older "Our Baby Registry" drafts use mock products with fake 4.x ratings, and those do show stars — the component itself works.)

So the missing piece is rating data, not the UI. There are two real ways to fix it:

input.questionnaire:
[topic] Stars fix
[question] How do you want star ratings to show up?
[option] Research real ratings into the catalog: I look up the current rating for each of the ~102 hand-picked catalog products and store them, so stars show locally with no API keys (snapshot values, like the stored prices; your existing registries would need a "Start over" to pick them up)
[option] Connect real retailer APIs: you add Amazon PA-API and/or Walmart affiliate keys to .env.local, and newly generated registries get live ratings straight from those stores
[option] Do both
[option] Leave it as is: stars appear automatically wherever a real rating exists
